paragrafos: **Three measurements side by side, never added together.** Two prediction markets (Polymarket and Kalshi), voting-intention polls checked against the official notice filed with the Commission des sondages, and French press coverage. The first round is on April 18 and the runoff on May 2, 2027.

**On 19/11/2026, the two markets and the polls measure different things about Marine Le Pen.** In the win contract, in the 00:45 UTC reading, Polymarket pays 47.75 and Kalshi 53.00. In the polls with fieldwork up to 13/11, she is first in all 76 first-round lists of the last 45 days, from 8 pollsters, with 27% to 38%, and she leads in the 35 runoff matchups in which she was tested, with 52% to 70%. The Ifop-Fiducial poll for TF1-LCI, Le Figaro and Sud Radio, with fieldwork from 13 to 16/11, already has an official notice, number 10384, and is not yet in the database. Her appeal against ineligibility at the Cour de cassation is due to be decided by early April 2027.

**Jean-Luc Mélenchon is 2nd in the poll average and 3rd in the Polymarket win contract.** In the polls, he averages 17.8 across 37 lists from 6 pollsters over the last 30 days and is among the top two in 70 of the 76 lists of the last 45 days; in the 12 runoff matchups in which he was tested, he trails in all of them, with 30% to 34%. In the win contract, he is at 14.50 on Polymarket and 12.00 on Kalshi.

**Two names in the top five of both markets appear in fewer than half of the lists in the poll database: David Lisnard in 31 of the 76 of the last 45 days, and Christine Lagarde in 2.** Lisnard is 2nd on Polymarket, at 17.65, and at 14.00 on Kalshi; in the polls, he is not among the top two in any of the 31 lists and averages 8.8 across 22 lists from 6 pollsters over the last 30 days. Lagarde is 5th on Polymarket, at 4.35, and at 5.00 on Kalshi; the two lists that test her are from Cluster17 for Politico, with fieldwork on 9 and 10/11, and give her 14% and 8%. Lagarde is not a declared candidate; on 29/10, the European Central Bank announced that she leaves the bank's presidency on 07/02/2027. Teddy Riner, who announced his candidacy on 09/11, is at 1.85 on Polymarket and 1.00 on Kalshi; he appears in 3 of the 76 lists, with 2% in the Cluster17 one, 4% in the OpinionWay one for CNews, with fieldwork from 10 to 12/11, and 4.5% in the Elabe one for BFMTV and La Tribune Dimanche, with fieldwork on 12 and 13/11.

**Édouard Philippe and Raphaël Glucksmann are less than one point apart in the poll average; in the Polymarket win contract, Philippe's price is more than three times Glucksmann's.** Philippe averages 13.0 over the last 30 days, across 25 lists from 6 pollsters, and Glucksmann 12.2, across 36 lists from 6 pollsters; in the lists of the last 45 days in which they appear, Philippe is among the top two in 3 of 52, and Glucksmann in 3 of 71. In the win contract, Philippe is at 5.50 on Polymarket and 5.20 on Kalshi, and Glucksmann at 1.55 and 2.00.

**In the 18:25 UTC press collection of 18/11, three of the ten headlines, from 8 outlets, are about polls published that day.** Two are from Le Figaro, which presents its poll: one on the first round, the other on a hypothetical primary of the right and centre. The first-round one is the Ifop-Fiducial poll for the paper, TF1-LCI and Sud Radio, with fieldwork from 13 to 16/11, which is not yet in the database and so is not on the screen. The RTL headline is about an Ifop poll for Franc-Tireur, with fieldwork from 2 to 4/11, on turnout in a runoff between Jean-Luc Mélenchon and Marine Le Pen; it does not measure voting intention. Le Parisien reports that David Lisnard and Bruno Retailleau are calling on Édouard Philippe to join the primary of the right and centre and are divided over Éric Zemmour taking part, and that Olympic boxing champion Estelle Mossely has joined Philippe's campaign team; Les Echos publishes an analysis saying that Philippe, "battered in the polls", is betting on his ideas to relaunch his campaign. BFMTV publishes a video in which Socialist MP Béatrice Bellay explains why she will not, after all, sponsor Teddy Riner's candidacy. Le Monde reports that the administrative court of Toulouse rejected Francis Lalanne's appeal against the mayor of Montauban, who cancelled the booking of the municipal hall where he was to hold a rally, and that Lalanne is keeping the rally, with Dieudonné attending. 20 Minutes reports that actor Jean Dujardin said, on a Québec radio station, that he is considering casting a blank vote in 2027.

**What this screen does not do.** It does not add or average the two markets, it does not turn a price into a voting intention, and it does not show a poll number without its checked official notice. On the Saturday and Sunday of each round, polls and prices are frozen, as French law of 1977 requires.
